questions.q: Where does the actual data live when you query it through Redshift Spectrum?
options: In S3 — it's never loaded onto the cluster's compute nodes
It's copied onto the leader node only
It's automatically copied into every compute node, same as a normal table
In DynamoDB, which Spectrum uses as an intermediate cache
questions.explain: Spectrum tables keep their definition in the catalog while the data itself stays in S3, read directly at query time.

questions.q: What does CREATE EXTERNAL SCHEMA ... FROM DATA CATALOG point at?
options: A Glue Data Catalog database — the same catalog Athena queries and Glue crawlers populate
A brand-new schema stored only inside Redshift, unrelated to Glue
An S3 bucket's IAM policy
A DMS replication instance
questions.explain: Spectrum external schemas map to a Glue Data Catalog database, so table definitions are shared with Athena rather than duplicated.

questions.q: Where does the scan-and-filter work for a Spectrum query actually run?
options: On a separate, AWS-managed Spectrum compute layer, outside your cluster's compute nodes
Entirely on the leader node
Entirely on your cluster's compute nodes, same as a normal table
On the client machine that issued the query
questions.explain: The Spectrum layer scales independently of your cluster and does the initial S3 scan/filter before handing results back for your cluster to finish.

questions.q: Based on this lesson, which use case fits Spectrum best?
options: Three years of rarely-queried historical data already cataloged in S3, queried maybe once a quarter
A small lookup table joined into nearly every query, needing guaranteed local access
Data that must have the absolute lowest, most predictable query latency at high frequency
A table that needs a custom DISTKEY for join performance
questions.explain: Spectrum fits data you want queryable without paying to store and load it repeatedly — cold, infrequently-queried data is the clearest case.

questions.q: Can a single query join a Spectrum (external) table against a normally-loaded Redshift table?
options: Yes — Spectrum tables behave like ordinary tables in SELECT, JOIN, and WHERE clauses
No — Spectrum tables can only be queried in complete isolation
Only if both tables share the same DISTKEY
Only through a separate Athena query, not directly in Redshift
questions.explain: Once an external schema exists, its tables can be referenced in ordinary SQL alongside regular Redshift tables, including joins.
